summary: Clarify throttling behavior for scheduled warmup spike causing 429s during off-peak batch jobs
description: Issue summary: Customer NexusSearch reports a recurring pattern of 429 throttles during a nightly scheduled warmup followed immediately by large batch imports. Impact: customer experiences sustained 429s for ~3-8 minutes after warmup, causing backoff storms and delayed batch completion. They are on a dedicated pool with autoscaling and a scheduled warmup job that runs at 03:00 UTC. They suspect warmup traffic is being counted against their tenant/burst quota and want guidance on configuration to avoid warmup-induced throttles.
impact: Batch imports delayed; retry storm increased downstream latency and job completion time. Customer reports a 15% SLA breach for nightly jobs on two recent dates (2026-03-08, 2026-03-09).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Dedicated pool tenant scheduled warmup at 03:00 UTC - lightweight sequence of concurrent chat starts (200 parallel short sessions)
2) Immediately after warmup (03:03 UTC) kick off bulk embedding job: 50 workers, parallel multipart uploads to embeddings endpoint
3) Observe 429s start ~03:03 and peak for ~3-8 minutes, then tail off as refill windows catch up
4) Repeatable on customer's prod pool; not observed in their staging (lower concurrency).
observed_behavior: 429 responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining dropping to 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset window aligned with midnight refill boundary. Metrics show a spike in token accounting during the warmup window followed by high rejected request rate during the subsequent batch window.
expected_behavior: Warmup traffic should not cause sustained tenant quota exhaustion for immediately following scheduled batch jobs. Guidance expected: configuration knobs to isolate or deprioritize warmup traffic, adjust burst credit allocation, or exclude warmup worker identities from quota accounting.
